identity_check: Confirmed as SiMa.ai (sima.ai; legal name SiMa Technologies, Inc. per the site footer), the San Jose, California company founded in 2018 by CEO Krishna Rangasayee that makes edge machine-learning chips (Modalix MLSoC family) plus the Palette software toolchain, now branded a 'Physical AI' platform. Every round page (company releases, Global Venturing, Fenwick, VentureBeat, TechStartups) names the same company and CEO. Not Sima (sima.co, other Sima-named startups) or any company named Sima Labs. Category kept remote (PROJECT_CONTEXT §7): SiMa sells silicon and an embedded-ML software stack to device makers (robots, cars, drones, lasers, machine vision); it does not sell agents for procurement, maintenance or process work to plant staff and has no design-intent or requirements product. It touches factories only as compute inside equipment (e.g. TRUMPF integrating its chips into laser systems, a Cisco 'Industry 4.0' edge collaboration). Layer kept autonomy_tooling as the compute/toolchain beneath autonomous machines; no layer fits a chip company exactly. Sector set to hardware_deeptech by model (the company calls itself a Physical AI platform, but the product is purpose-built silicon).

layer_detail: Edge compute layer: Modalix MLSoC chips and dev kits plus the Palette / Palette Neat software environment for deploying vision, multimodal and generative models on robots, humanoids, cars, drones and factory equipment
product_summary: Sells the Modalix family of machine-learning systems-on-chip and development kits, paired with Palette, a software suite (now with an agentic environment, Palette Neat) that compiles and deploys AI models on the chip. Pitched as low-power on-device inference for robotics, automotive, drones, aerospace, industrial automation and smart vision.

open_items: Seed: the Series A pages say total raised reached $40M with the $30M Series A, implying about $10M of earlier funding, but no page read describes a seed round (amount, date or investors). Not recorded as a round.
Series B1 first tranche (before the October 2022 extension): date and investors not found; recorded as one $67M B1 round at the extension date.
June 2023 $13M: series not named; VentureTech Alliance (TSMC-affiliated Taiwan fund) is the only investor TechStartups names.
Micron strategic investment (Apr 2026): amount not disclosed.
Valuations before the Series C not disclosed on pages read; The Information (May 2026, listed on sima.ai/news) reported the company raising at $1.4B, article paywalled and not read.

Named customers: the company groups customers and partners together ('customer and partner network ... including ARK Electronics, AVerMedia, Bosch, Emerson, Intrinsic, Kontron, L&T Technology Services, Micron, STIGA, Synopsys, TRUMPF SE, and Virya Autonomous Technologies'); none is explicitly called a customer, so named_customers is left empty. TRUMPF is integrating SiMa.ai chips into its laser systems (Jul 2024 partnership).

Revenue not publicly reported in figures; the Series C release says only that revenue growth 'quadrupled' year over year between 2024 and 2025. TechStartups (Jun 2023) quoted 'more than 50 customers' testing its chips.
Headcount: only 'approximately 200 employees' (TRUMPF release, Jul 2024) found; no current figure.
BusinessWire originals of the 2020 Series A and 2021 Series B releases returned 403; Economic Times, Mint and Forbes coverage of the Series C / B1 could not be fetched.
